title: Bench-test heuristics and quick debrief — Sikha Patel (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick, informal scratchpad for synthesizing the bench test + interview thread for Sikha Patel. Not polished. Use this to seed the formal scorecard and hiring comms.

TL;DR summary:
- Strong systems intuition around batching and KV cache; weaker on quantization tradeoffs (especially fp16 vs int8 artifacts).
- Code test: solved core problem but missed a couple of pathological latency cases; implementation readable but not instrumented for production metrics.
- Culture/operating fit: high marks on cross-team communication examples, pragmatic about tradeoffs.

Context and timeline:
- Take-home bench test given 2025-10-15 (latency-sensitive transformer serving micro-benchmark).
- Pairing session (1:1 live code + design) on 2025-11-01 (~75m).
- Followup async notes from candidate on 2025-11-03 with small patch to address concurrency bug.

Candidate quick profile:
- Name: Sikha Patel
- Seniority: Senior Software/ML Infra Engineer (IC4-ish)
- Current: mid-stage startup (infra team) with direct experience shipping serving infra and profiling kernels.

Bench-test notes (concrete):
1) Correctness: core algorithm works. Implemented a continuous-batching loop, preserved ordering guarantees. Unit tests pass (small corpus).
2) Latency stability: observed 95th p95 spikes in synthetic harness when concurrency > 32. Candidate's approach did not protect against head-of-line blocking in the task queue — missing timeout/backpressure config.
3) Resource efficiency: uses simple pooling; memory safety OK. Did not include adaptive batching heuristics or dynamic batch size based on sequence length distribution.
4) Observability: minimal — added print-based timing. No structured traces/metrics (op-level latencies, token emit times).
5) Edge cases: retry semantics were naive — potential double-send on transient worker failure. Candidate addressed with a followup patch that added idempotency key usage (good catch).

Technical reasoning observed in pairing:
- Strong mental model of KV cache invalidation and why cross-request sharing can reduce repeated decoding work. Could sketch how to shard cache by model-version + session id. Good intuition.
- When asked about quantization, defaulted to saying "we can quantize and expect some perf gain" but could not articulate expected numerical tradeoffs for int8 GPUs vs 16-bit kernels or how to detect quantization-induced hallucination regressions.
- Comfortable with kernel-level profiling (nvprof-like flow) and identified where memcpy-to-device dominated small-sequence workloads. Proposed batched memcpy optimization but didn't quantify speedups live.

Behavioral / collaboration signals:
- Explains tradeoffs to non-ops stakeholders clearly (gave an example PR where they summarized latency vs cost tradeoffs for product PM).
- Played well with feedback in pairing — accepted a suggestion to add instrumentation and iterated quickly.
- Mentions prior experience owning an on-call rota and writing a postmortem for an inference outage (concrete).

Preliminary heuristic score (0-5 scale, my quick gut):
- Systems design (serving/runtime): 4
- Production hygiene (metrics, testing, idempotency): 3
- Kernel/hw optimization knowledge: 3
- Collaboration & communication: 5
- Overall hire inclination: Lean+: likely to hire for IC4 given mentorship, but would want an early ramp plan focused on quantization and production tracing.

Red flags / gaps to call out explicitly:
- Lacks strong quantization story and eval methodology for quality regressions (need to probe: how would they set up an automated regression suite tied to prompt families?).
- Implementation missing backpressure/timeouts; could lead to p95 regressions in production under sudden load changes.
- Observability: minimal; would need to pair on instrumentation standards.

Suggested followups (actionable):
- Ask candidate to sketch a short RFC (~1 page) on "safe quantization rollout for our serving stack": include detection (eval sets), rollback criteria, and perf measurement plan. Give 4–5 days to complete. This will show both technical depth and product-aware tradeoffs.
- Small take-home: extend their bench harness to measure candidate's proposed memcpy-batching optimization end-to-end (we can give them the harness repo link). Accepts code + short bench report.
- Reference check: ask about a specific outage mentioned in interview; request to see the postmortem or a summary that highlights their role.

Draft Slack blurb for hiring channel (short):
"Sikha Patel — senior infra engineer. Solid systems instincts, excellent communicator; shipped readable code in bench test. Needs stronger quantization + observability experience for infra runtime role. Recommend next step: short RFC and small bench extension to validate quantization/eval thinking. Lean+ hire pending those artifacts."

Notes-to-self / interview artifacts:
- PR to review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-tests/pull/527 (candidate's patch + my inline comments)
- Pairing replay: saved vim history + minimal logs in /tmp/bench-sikha-{date} on my laptop (todo: upload to shared drive if we proceed).

Open questions to resolve before final score:
- How would Sikha detect subtle quality regressions after int8 quantization? Ask for specific metrics and thresholds.
- What monitoring signals would trigger an automatic fallback to non-quantized variant? (latency-only? quality-only? both?)
- Timezone / ramp concerns: candidate currently in IST — confirm overlap windows for on-call and sync cadence.

Next steps (if moving forward):
1) Send RFC prompt (deadline: 5 business days).
2) Provide harness + small task for memcpy batching; expect bench results + patch (deadline: 7 business days).
3) Run reference check focused on SRE ownership and postmortem example.

Final quick gut: positive. Not a plug-and-play runbook lead day-1, but great for a Senior runtime role with a 2–3 month ramp focused on quantization and tracing.

-- Rubin
(p.s. saving this as scratch — will distill into the canonical panel scorecard if Priya/Evan want to discuss)
